subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In jazz, the term 'swing' refers to:
options: An uneven, lilting rhythmic feel where quavers are played long-short
questions.explain: Swing gives a relaxed, lilting feel by playing pairs of quavers as long-short rather than even.

questions.q: In the circle of fifths, how many sharps are in the key signature of D major?
questions.explain: D major has two sharps (F sharp and C sharp) in its key signature.

questions.q: Which Caribbean style, associated with Trinidad, often features witty topical lyrics and syncopated rhythms?
questions.explain: Calypso, from Trinidad, is known for its witty, topical lyrics and syncopated rhythms.

questions.q: A repeated rhythmic or melodic pattern, common in world and minimalist music, is an:
questions.explain: An ostinato is a persistently repeated musical pattern.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: Compared with a major scale, a (natural) minor key generally sounds:
questions.explain: Minor keys typically sound darker or sadder than the brighter major.

questions.q: Which Italian dynamic term means 'very quiet'?
questions.explain: Pianissimo (pp) means very quiet, whereas fortissimo (ff) means very loud.

questions.q: What is 'syncopation'?
options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

questions.q: 'Theme and variations' form is one in which:
options: A single chord is held throughout
A theme is stated then repeated with changes each time
questions.explain: In theme and variations a main theme is stated then repeated in altered forms.

questions.q: A short, catchy repeated instrumental phrase in pop and rock is called a:
questions.explain: A riff is a short, repeated, catchy instrumental phrase, common in rock and pop.

questions.q: Which of these is a string instrument of the orchestra?
questions.explain: The cello belongs to the string family; clarinet is woodwind and trumpet is brass.

questions.q: Roughly which dates define the Classical period?
questions.explain: The Classical period spans roughly 1750 to 1820.

questions.q: What does 'rit.' (ritardando) mean?
questions.explain: Ritardando means to gradually slow the tempo down.

questions.q: Which chords does a standard 12-bar blues use?
questions.explain: The 12-bar blues is built on the primary chords I, IV and V.

questions.q: During which period did the orchestra grow largest, adding instruments like the tuba and cor anglais?
questions.explain: The Romantic period saw the orchestra expand greatly with new and additional instruments.

questions.q: 'Composing to a brief' means:
options: Composing music to meet a given set of requirements or purpose
questions.explain: Composing to a brief means writing music that fulfils a specified purpose or set of instructions.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: The harmonic minor scale differs from the natural minor by raising which note?
questions.explain: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh note by a semitone, creating a leading note.

questions.q: A standard Classical symphony usually has how many movements?
questions.explain: A typical Classical symphony has four movements, often fast-slow-minuet-fast.

questions.q: Which Italian tempo term means 'fast and lively'?
questions.explain: Allegro means fast and lively, whereas adagio and largo are slow.

questions.q: Which 20th-century technique uses all twelve chromatic notes in a fixed order with none repeated?
questions.explain: Serialism, or twelve-tone technique, orders all twelve pitches into a row used as the basis of a piece.
